items.title: Brands are buying viral posts as ads (Startup idea)
items.summary:
Good morning.
Google released 3.8 Flash... I tried it with my Hermes agent... it's insanely fast. Made me have a realization about Google's approach.
This model will be a daily driver that powers agents. It won't be heavy or deep thinking for long loops, but it will get work done.
Grok 4.7 is coming next week.
The builders are the winners in this model race. Take advantage.
Estimated reading time: 3 minutes 12 seconds

items.title: Sell brands the viral posts they can boost
items.summary:
Why now
TikTok's
Content Suite
already shows viral videos with spark codes that brands can boost.
It's proven content that they don't have to create.
The problem: Getting the codes is still DMs, one creator at a time.
The product
Be their content pipeline salesmen. You bring posts their own customers already made, cleared and ready to run. You pay the creator, the brand pays you more.
Twenty posts about their product, sorted by views.
What each creator wants for 30 days of ad rights.
The code, ready to paste into Ads Manager.
The date each one expires, so they know when to re-up.
How I’d start
Pick one brand with a lot of organic mentions.

items.title: How to find money in dead leads
items.summary:
Good morning.
Job postings are starting to read a lot like creator business plans.
a16z crypto is hiring a social media lead for $199K to $232K.
They want someone chronically online who gets internet culture, crypto, can create and ship across: Podcasts, Investments, Events, Editorial, Memes, Clips, Social strategy.
Sounds more like a business than a job.
I think they want to hire the next
Threadguy
(who is a legend - watch his stream)
You could prob make $1M/yr partnering with a16z and other brands.
Estimated reading time: 3 minutes 30 seconds

items.title: Run the refund desk contractors don't have
items.summary:
Why now
Contractors get billed for leads that never had a chance. Dead number. Wrong trade. Two hours outside the service area.
A home service lead runs $90.92 on average, $228.15 in roofing. A dead one costs the same as a booked job.
Thumbtack
refunds all of those
. They just make you file each one by hand, one at a time, in the app.
Nobody running a truck is doing that on a Tuesday night. Google already automated this away. Thumbtack still makes it your problem.
Cost per lead by trade.

items.title: Enterprise software giants are moving down market.
items.summary:
Enterprise products and pricing is moving downstream toward individuals, flexibility and agents.
HubSpot's co-founder Dharmesh Shah just shipped a $1 CRM built for you. The stock went up 10% last week...
HubSpot's average customer pays
$11,800
a year.
Salesforce is moving away from 3 year enterprise deals and toward a meter (new partnership buying
m3ter
)
They'll start charging for work instead of seats.
I'm keeping an eye on this.
The big guys come down market they get good at pricing very fast.
What they can't buy is an ear to the street.
